keyVerseText: Again I say unto you, That if two of you shall agree on earth as touching any thing that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father which is in heaven.
rootMeaning: The word συμφωνέω (symphōnéō) derives from the root σύμφωνος (sýmphōnos), which literally means 'consent' or 'sounding together.' This etymology highlights the concept of harmony or agreement in sound, implying a unity or accord that is more than mere coincidence. Beyond the common English gloss of 'agree,' the root sense conveys a deep, harmonious concord, as when musical notes blend in unison, suggesting a spiritual or relational unity that is fitting and deliberate.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, συμφωνέω is used six times and translated variously as 'shall agree,' 'when he had agreed,' 'didst,' 'agreeth,' 'have agreed together,' and simply 'agree.' This range of translations shows the word's flexibility in expressing both the act of coming to agreement and the state of being in harmony, whether in opinion, purpose, or arrangement. Its consistent use to denote agreement underscores the importance of unity and accord in the biblical narrative, whether in human relationships or divine-human interaction.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, συμφωνέω reveals the biblical emphasis on unity and harmony among believers and between humanity and God. This word's original meaning of 'sounding together' invites believers to reflect on the spiritual reality of concord that mirrors the perfect harmony found in God's nature. Such agreement is not merely external but involves a heart-level accord that aligns with God's will. Understanding συμφωνέω enriches the Christian faith by highlighting how God calls His people into a unified community that reflects His own harmonious character, fostering peace, cooperation, and mutual edification.
keyVerseReflection: Matthew 18:19 states, 'Again I say unto you, That if two of you shall agree on earth as touching any thing that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father which is in heaven.' Here, συμφωνέω emphasizes the power and significance of believers being in harmonious agreement in prayer. The word conveys more than simple concurrence; it suggests a spiritual unity that aligns with the Father's will, making their requests effective. This verse encourages believers to seek true accord, trusting that God honors such united faith.
